key_insight: Synthetic AI data in biomedicine has grown rapidly over the past decade, but real-world translation remains limited, especially outside imaging and molecular research.
clinical_relevance: The work suggests synthetic data could help address scarcity and privacy barriers, but clinical use is still rare and needs stronger evaluation before broader adoption.
method: Bibliometric analysis with expert annotation and LLM-assisted classification
Tracked modality, medical domain, paper type, deployment status, and research stance
evidence_signal: Publication volume increased steadily, 77.8% of papers were strongly supportive, only 27 reported operational use, and critical studies were under 1%.
watch_item: The evidence base is publication-heavy but deployment-light, so performance claims may not yet reflect routine clinical or operational settings.
paper_title: AI-Based Synthetic Data in Biomedicine: A Decade of Growth and a Persistent Translation Gap
